sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Wayland, or Wieland, is a hero of British myth and folklore. Like the Irish Goban Saor, he is a relic of an older mythological figure. The smith held powers beyond ordinary people in Celtic and German belief alike. The limp of Wayland may have arrived from the Mediterranean, whose smith god Vulcan was pictured with a limp. King Nithland, ruler of the Niars, cut his hamstrings so he could not leave the forge. Wayland answered by killing the king's son and taking his daughter. He also forged blades of great worth, among them Excalibur, the sword of Arthur.

okr.objective: Present Wayland as a supernatural smith of British folklore.
